newsitem.title: USA: US money managers shorten US debt positions-survey.
newsitem.headline: US money managers shorten US debt positions-survey.

text.p: Portfolio managers continued to take more-defensive positions in U.S. debt markets in the past week, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
"Overall, money managers in the survey are flat, but there is a more-defensive bias imbedded in some of the larger portfolios," the report said.

In the week ended December 17, the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading rose to 4.98 from 4.97 the prior week; the asset-weighted number rose to 5.26 from 4.68 in the week ended December 10, according to the report.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio rose to 6.63 percent from 6.47 percent.
Duration bogey rose to 4.22 on an arithmetic basis and 4.93 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

Eight percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from 20 percent the week before. The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active was 6.0, up from 5.0 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
